The test image shows tomato leaves with:
- Overall bronzed/silvery-green discoloration
- Numerous small brown necrotic spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Some leaf curling/distortion
- Spots appear to have blurred, indistinct margins

This pattern strongly suggests **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (bronzing + necrotic spots with blurred margins) or possibly **Powdery_Mildew** or **Leaf_Mold**. Let me check the part index and then view reference images.
Affected part is **leaf**. Top candidates from leaf index: Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Powdery_Mildew, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Verticillium_Wilt. Now viewing one reference from each top candidate.
This TSWV reference shows ring/concentric patterns - doesn't match well with the test image's diffuse bronzing. Let me check Powdery_Mildew.
Powdery Mildew shows white powdery spots - doesn't match the test image. Let me check Septoria_Leaf_Blotch.
Septoria shows large dark blotches - doesn't match the fine bronzing/stippling pattern. Let me view the 4th reference: Verticillium_Wilt.

Verticillium Wilt shows V-shaped lesion with yellow border - doesn't match.

**Analysis summary:**

| Reference | Visual | Match? |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| TSWV | Ring/concentric patterns, some necrosis | Partial - bronzing matches but rings don't |
| Powdery Mildew | White powdery circular spots | No |
| Septoria | Large dark blotches with yellowing | No |
| Verticillium Wilt | V-shaped brown lesion, yellow margin | No |

**Test image key features:**
- Diffuse bronzed/teal-green discoloration of the entire leaf surface
- Fine, uniformly scattered small brown necrotic spots with blurred margins
- Some leaf curling/distortion
- No distinct ring patterns, white coating, or V-shaped lesions

The TSWV symptom description specifically calls out "bronzing on upper leaf surfaces, distinct necrotic spots, downward-cupped leaves" and "lesions caused by TSWV have blurred margins." The test image aligns with this - the bronzed leaf surface with fine scattered spots with indistinct margins is characteristic of TSWV, even though the ring pattern reference wasn't a perfect match (rings are more a fruit/green tomato manifestation).
